newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Monday, with bearish Malaysian crop data keeping buyers sidelined, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,380-85 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at five rupiah below the range. Crude palm oil was done at 1,179 rupiah/kg and 1,181 rupiah at a tender for two parcels of 500 tonnes each in the North Sumatran capital of Medan on Monday.
"The market was not very active following declines in Malaysia after the PORLA report," one trader said. "I think prices will remain under pressure tomorrow."
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put end-May palm oil stocks at 711,841 tonnes, compared with 699,423 tonnes at end-April.
It said crude palm oil output rose 7.61 percent to 790,640 tonnes in May from 734,694 tonnes in April, while May palm oil exports rose to 626,606 tonnes from 579,211 tonnes in April.

"I think the Malaysian market will carry a bearish tone in the short term," one trader said. "The growth in production from April to May was higher than the growth in exports in the same months while stocks grew by nearly 1.80 percent."
